q1Derivation.rule: Owner Clarification Q1: obligations are served in ascending selectionIndex order; reserves are assigned in ascending frozen rank order
q1Derivation.derivationNote: sorted here by selectionIndex ascending over the two CURRENT_ACQUISITION_FAILURE slots. planPendingReplacementObligations was NOT used as the ordering authority; it was used only to derive reserve POSITIONS once the order was fixed, and its output was compared against the independently derived order

previousQ1IsNotCarriedForward.whyItIsStale: slot 29 closed successfully in Window 02 and slot 51 closed successfully in the recovery. Carrying the old queue forward would serve two slots that owe nothing and would spend two reserves for no reason

q1Derivation.whyNoSlot59Obligation: P:59 has not been adjudicated unsuccessful. An obligation carries a Q3 reason, and creating one would decide the question the bound owner decision deliberately leaves open
notConsulted: how many times a slot has already been replaced

reserveAssignmentDerivation.everyPositionPreviouslyUnassigned: ledger entry k consumes position k for k in 0..18; positions 19 and 20 appear in no committed entry
reserveAssignmentDerivation.ownerTaskIsNotTheAuthority: the assignments above were derived from the validated ledger and the frozen draw. The owner task's list agreed on both, but the derivation - not the task text - is what this record binds
reserveAssignmentDerivation.positionsAreIndependentOfIdentity: a position was assigned before any reserve draw entry was read. Only after each position was fixed was draw.reserve[position] looked up, mechanically
reserveAssignmentDerivation.chainLengthDoesNotAffectPosition: slot 45 is on its THIRD occupant and slot 54 on its second. Ascending selectionIndex still decides the order and the next unused positions still follow monotonically

selectedOption.derivation: STEP 1-5 of the resumed authority's DETERMINATE_Q1_REPLACEMENTS_BEFORE_NEW_PRIMARIES algorithm. Two determinate obligations exist, so they take positions 1 and 2; the remaining three positions are filled with the next never-started primaries in ascending order, skipping nothing and including no pending slot
selectedOption.whyNotFivePrimaries: the resumed authority requires determinate Q1 replacements before new primaries. Leaving 45 and 54 unserved while starting five fresh slots would grow the open-obligation set rather than close it
selectedOption.whyNotTwoItemsOnly: the window size is exactly 5 whenever at least five executable work items remain, and 50 never-started primaries remain

candidateWindow.everyDrawEntrySha256RecomputedHere: each digest is drawEntrySha256 of the frozen draw entry itself - draw.reserve[19] and draw.reserve[20] for the replacements, draw.selection[60..62] for the primaries. Recomputed in this step from the bound draw file, not copied from any earlier record
candidateWindow.splitsAreTheSELECTIONSLOTSSplits: a replacement inherits the SLOT's split, not a split of its own: the reserve occupies slot 45 and slot 54, both DEV_CONFIRM. This is what the landed spec validator checks

frozenSplitCrossCheck.holdoutHandling: P:60 is FINAL_HOLDOUT. Its acquisition proceeds exactly as any other item, and its page evidence is never inspected, summarised or described in any record. Only structural counts appear

derivedThresholds.p2Derivation: strictPercentThresholdCount(5, 40) = 3 - the smallest count strictly above 40% of 5
derivedThresholds.p5Derivation: strictPercentThresholdCount(5, 30) = 2 - the smallest count strictly above 30% of 5
derivedThresholds.windowLocalCountersStartAtZero: P1, P2, P3 and P5 counters are FRESH for this window. Window 02's P5 count is NOT carried forward (Owner Clarification Q4). P6 remains generation-global and P7 remains immediate

plannedLedgerTransition.everyFieldIsDerivedByPrepareReplacementA: the replaced occupant, previousSequenceForSlot, previousEntryHash and split are all derived by the landed builder from the ledger and the draw. This record states what the builder MUST produce so that a disagreement is visible, not values that are fed to it

slot45.isThisConcerning: it is recorded, not concealed. The slot has now been refused by three distinct occupants for three distinct reasons - two host-unreachable and one readable-robots disallow. No rule caps the chain length, and the reserve pool has 21 unused positions. If this slot continues to consume reserves it becomes an owner question, but it is not one yet

failureSemantics.aFailedReplacementCreatesAQ2SameSlotObli: if R:45:19 or R:54:20 is adjudicated unsuccessful, that SAME slot owes another replacement, which would sort into the next window's Q1 by ascending selectionIndex
failureSemantics.aFailedPrimaryCreatesAnObligationForItsO: if P:60, P:61 or P:62 is adjudicated unsuccessful, that selection slot owes a replacement
failureSemantics.anAddressPolicyRefusalIsNotAutomatically: the bound operational vantage rule is applied FIRST. If all five of its clauses are proved, the run is preserved as environment evidence, the occupant is HELD, no obligation is created, no reserve is assigned, and the window STOPS for review. If any clause is unproved, ordinary frozen Q3 governs
failureSemantics.anSD7RangeStraddlingTheThresholdIsNotAFa: it is PENDING_CAPABILITY_REVIEW: no replacement obligation, and a stop

knownAdapterLimitations.forgedSuccessCount: the adapter checks the success count only through P6 consistency. At a 19-entry ledger P6 requires successes >= 50 to be NOT_TRIGGERED, so any forged value at or above 50 passes. This is a landed limitation recorded in earlier windows; the defence is that the count is derived independently in this record and re-derived at adjudication, never read from an adapter
knownAdapterLimitations.spentStrategyReplay: the adapter accepts a spent strategy replayed against a ledger revision that still matches its own binding, because the ledger records no success. Window-02's strategy binds the fifteen-entry ledger and so cannot bind here; but a strategy whose window paused before appending could be replayed. The defence is procedural - a spent strategy is marked spent and never re-fed

negativeProbes.executedAgainst: the exact committed strategy bytes, mutated one probe at a time, fed to the landed windowSpecFromAcquisitionWindowStrategy against the real 19-entry ledger

positiveControl.note: the unmutated strategy binds a spec whose work items, splits, reserve positions, replacement reasons and derived occupant kinds are exactly the ones this record precommits

negativeProbes.theOneAcceptedProbeIsNotANewDefect: probe 9 was PREDICTED to be accepted and is recorded as a known landed adapter limitation, not as a passing check. It is the same limitation earlier windows recorded. The defence is structural rather than adapter-side: the success count is derived independently in this record from a 110-slot status map, and is re-derived from scratch at adjudication. No step in this window reads a success count from the adapter
